title: Asiya's arms
hook: Pharaoh's wife finds the baby and says: a joy for me and you, do not kill him
carry: a good heart in a hard house

segments.voice: Yesterday: tabut, the chest on the river, a mother opening her hands at the water's edge. Your line was put it on the river. Did one worry float, even for a while? Day forty-four.

A gentle parent raised by a harsh one. A coworker who stays decent in an office where nobody else bothers. Kindness doesn't always come from the house a person is in. Sometimes they carry it in themselves. The river carries the chest downstream, and where does it wash up? Of all the places in Egypt, at Pharaoh's own palace. His household lifts it from the water. Inside is a baby boy, exactly the kind of baby Pharaoh has ordered killed. And then a woman steps forward and puts herself between the baby and the man who gives the orders. Today: Asiya's arms.
screen: `KINDNESS FROM A HARD HOUSE.` → `THE CHEST REACHES THE PALACE.` → `A WOMAN STEPS FORWARD.`

segments.voice: Surah al-Qasas again. Pharaoh's household picks the baby up, and the wife of Pharaoh says: a delight of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him. Perhaps he will be of use to us, or we may take him as a son. The Arabic for delight of the eye is qurratu 'ayn, literally coolness of the eye. One old explanation: in a hot land, a cool eye is a happy one, resting on something it loves. She looks at a baby her husband has sentenced to death and sees her delight, and says so, to his face, and adds: do not kill him. The Qur'an doesn't give her name. Muslim tradition calls her Asiya, and honors her. Her faith shows up later, in Surah at-Tahrim, where the Qur'an holds her up as an example for believers. She prays: my Lord, build for me a home with You in the Garden, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds. The queen of Egypt, in a palace, asking for a different house. And the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, in a hadith in Bukhari, named her among the women who reached perfection, alongside Maryam, the mother of 'Isa. Two women in two very different houses, and both remembered for the same thing: a heart that stayed turned toward Allah whatever the walls around it were like. So this is how the child who will one day stand against Pharaoh grows up: in Pharaoh's house, held by Pharaoh's wife. The rescue walked in through the front door.
screen: `A DELIGHT OF THE EYE.` · `DO NOT KILL HIM.` · `A HOME WITH YOU IN THE GARDEN.` · `AMONG THE WOMEN OF PERFECTION.` · then, large: `QURRATU 'AYN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: protect someone small today. Settle, and breathe. Think of who, around you, has the least power. A child. A new hire. The quiet one in the group chat who gets talked over. An animal. An elderly neighbor. Picture one of them, and picture a moment today when you might be the one who says, do not. Don't interrupt them. Don't leave them out. Don't make the joke at their expense. Just one sentence, said out loud when it counts. If you pray, you can ask for a steady voice. The bell holds the time.
Asiya's arms. The wife of Pharaoh, who held the baby her husband wanted dead and said: do not kill him. Today's word.
Your line: a good heart in a hard house. Wherever you are that's hard today, bring in one kindness that wasn't there before. Day forty-four.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, as a woman of faith the Qur'an itself holds up as an example, and some recite her prayer from Surah at-Tahrim in times of hardship.

fork.reveal: Pharaoh's wife says: a delight of the eye for me and for you. do not kill him. the future prophet grows up in the house of the man he'll one day stand against.

original.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 28:9: "coolness of the eye," a delight — what Asiya called the baby.

trapdoor: what you thought: a kind princess finds a baby.
what it means: Pharaoh's own wife defends the baby he wants dead, and later prays to be saved from Pharaoh and his deeds.
what a scholar hears: the Qur'an never names her; tradition calls her Asiya, and a hadith in Bukhari names her with Maryam among the women who reached perfection.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3411 (many men reached perfection, and of women only Maryam and Asiya)

notes: Hadith number (Bukhari 3411) cited from memory; the hadith also mentions 'A'isha's excellence. Some versions (e.g. Tirmidhi) add Khadija and Fatima. The script says 'among the women who reached perfection, alongside Maryam'. Confirm.

Exodus names Pharaoh's daughter as the one who finds the baby; the Qur'an says his wife. The script does not compare; the trapdoor's first floor ('a kind princess') gestures at the popular picture only.
'Coolness of the eye' explanation (cool eye = happy eye in Arab idiom) is the standard lexical note; confirm.
